newsitem.title: USA: State beef group paints favorable consumer outlook.
newsitem.headline: State beef group paints favorable consumer outlook.

text.p: Consumers will continue to enjoy favorable beef prices during 1997, thanks to ample competitive meat supplies and liquidation that will boost beef production, the Minnesota Beef Council (MBC) said Friday.

"With record or near-record meat and poultry production expected in 1997, retail beef prices will probably continue to trend lower," Ron Eustice, MBC executive director, said in a statement. Eustice could not be reached for comment.
Eustice said fed cattle prices will likely range from $62 to $66 per cwt in the first quarter of 1997, $58 to $64 in the second, $63 to $68 in the third and $68 to $72 in the fourth.

Continued herd liquidation will pressure prices, and Eustice estimated 1997 U.S. beef production near 25.7 billion pounds, one percent above the 25.5 billion pounds produced in 1996 and second only to the record 26.0 billion pounds in 1976.

"This will be the seventh consecutive year of high beef production and will put per-capita consumption near 67 pounds on a retail weight basis. Per capita beef consumption has increased during each of the past three years," Eustice said.
"It will probably be late 1997 or early 1998 before supplies will tighten enough to cause any substantial increase in prices," he said.
Pork and poultry will continue to offer stiff competition to beef prices, Eustice said.

He estimated 1997 pork production near 17.3 billion pounds, up slightly from 17.1 billion pounds in 1996. Poultry production was expected to increase three percent to 32.6 billion pounds, compared with 31.6 billion pounds in 1996, Eustice said.
